ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The main body in the figure is a fused aromatic heterocycle, with a benzene ring on the left and a pyridine-like ring containing one ring nitrogen on the right, overall corresponding to a quinoline skeleton. The side chain is connected to the aromatic carbon adjacent to the ring nitrogen in this nitrogen-containing aromatic ring. After ignoring the curved arrows in the figure, the side-chain central carbon is connected to the aromatic-ring carbon, one NH2, and two OH groups. Reasoning: Encoding according to connectivity, the side chain can be written as N-C(O)(O)-aryl, where the central carbon is a tetracoordinate tetrahedral carbon. The aryl part is represented by a valid quinoline aromatic SMILES, with the connection point at the ortho position to the ring nitrogen, which can be written as c1ccc2ccccc2n1. Therefore the complete SMILES is NC(O)(O)c1ccc2ccccc2n1.

method.method_draft: First parse only the connectivity in the image, ignoring all curved arrows. Recognize the fused aromatic heterocycle as quinoline and note that the side chain is attached at the aromatic carbon next to the ring nitrogen. Then encode the side-chain carbon as a tetrahedral carbon bonded to NH2, two hydroxyl oxygens, and that quinoline carbon: N-C(O)(O)-aryl. Finally append a valid aromatic quinoline SMILES for the attached ring, giving NC(O)(O)c1ccc2ccccc2n1.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the single direct route: visually identify the molecular graph in the drawing and encode that graph as a canonical/acceptable SMILES while ignoring curved arrows. No alternative data or computation is needed.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as a fused benzene–pyridine aromatic system with one ring nitrogen (quinoline-like core). Identify the substituent on the carbon adjacent to the ring nitrogen: a single tetrahedral carbon bonded to the quinoline carbon, to NH2, and to two OH groups. Treat the curved arrows and transition-state motion marks as annotations, not atoms or bonds.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard skeletal-structure-to-SMILES rules: unlabeled aromatic ring vertices are carbons written as lowercase c; the ring nitrogen is aromatic n; explicit heteroatom substituents are N and O; the central sp3 carbon attached to NH2, two OH groups, and the aromatic carbon is written as C(O)(O) with N as another branch/neighbor. Encode the quinoline core with fused-ring closure syntax such as c1ccc2ccccc2n1.
